key_insight: Halide ordering—not just composition—strongly controls miscibility and structural phase transitions in mixed-halide perovskites, shifting transition temperatures by up to 100 K.
engineering_relevance: This means perovskite solar-cell stability and phase behavior can be tuned by managing halide distribution and A-site cation choice, not only by selecting the nominal stoichiometry.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) on DFT reference data for mixed Cs/Rb lead halide perovskites.
Ran large-scale hybrid Monte Carlo–molecular dynamics simulations to sample both configurational and vibrational degrees of freedom.
Compared Br-Cl, Br-I, and Cl-I systems across temperature to map miscibility gaps and ordering-driven phase boundaries.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that all three binary halide systems show miscibility gaps, with ordering appearing from 200 K to 500 K and a strong, composition-dependent shift in the orthorhombic-tetragonal boundary in CsPbBr3yI3-3y.
watch_item: Results depend on the accuracy and transferability of the MLIPs and on how well the simulated compositions and temperature range represent operating device conditions.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
